title: update Hugo theme to Graphite
description:
This PR updates the base Hugo theme to [Graphite](https://github.com/rstudio/hugo-graphite). It also:

+ bumps our Hugo version on Netlify to `0.71.1` (to allow the [header links](https://gohugo.io/getting-started/configuration-markup#heading-link-example))
+ upgrades the netlify.toml structure
+ restricts TOC printing to level 2 headers only (so `## Acknowledgements` will show up, but not `### Acknowledgements`)


Here is what is new with the theme:

## Theme update 2020.07.01 

### New and improved features include:

* Gains tags for each blog post
* Gains new taxonomy terms templates for [tags](https://hugo-graphite.netlify.app/tags/) and [categories](https://hugo-graphite.netlify.app/categories/)
* Gains a sticky Table of Contents for blog posts
* Gains copy-to-clipboard functionality for code chunks
* Gains anchorized header links
* Gains new shortcodes to create note and warning boxes
* Gains two new layout types ([**tutorial**](https://hugo-graphite.netlify.app/start/) and [**learn**](https://hugo-graphite.netlify.app/learn/))
* Better image accessibility
* Larger base font sizes for improved accessibility
* Many more parameters for customizing the site aesthetics

### Small tweaks

* Adds `target=_blank` to all external links
* Hexes on package pages are now symmetric
* Improved functioning for highlighting active menu items in the upper navbar (even with Hugo [nested sections](https://gohugo.io/content-management/sections/#nested-sections))
* JQuery upgrade
* Improved RSS feed handling (see: https://hugo-graphite.netlify.app/blog/index.xml)
* Improved sharing images for opengraph and twitter
* Styled footnotes from Goldmark Renderer
* Includes chroma CSS styles for highlighting via downlit for Hugodown sites
* Shiny new [demo site](https://hugo-graphite.netlify.app/)
* A new Hugo theme name that people can actually pronounce!

title: Draft learning content for edu home page
description:
Here's a draft of my concept of the home page. It begins with an overview of why we're here, followed by a section which has our latest video content, and then 6 subsections, most of which are targeted at a persona. Two of the personas I targeted--pro product users and certified instructors--don't exist in our current persona list, but feel important enough for our commercial work to target. A final section points off to a list of resources, which I intend to include both our own and community resources.

I haven't filled in any of the branch pages, which is where most of the detail will lie. I was just trying to communicate the overall framework as you suggested.

I have unsplash images for all the sections, but I'm hoping for original artwork instead. :-)

I mocked up the concept that I coded in Markdown in Pages; here's a PDF of the sort of idea I was aiming for.

[mockup.pdf](https://github.com/rstudio/education.rstudio.com/files/3149669/mockup.pdf)

See what you think.
-C
